0._section_summary: This abstract describes a single study examining relationships between interoceptive awareness (IA) and body image in community adults. The study included 646 British adults (447 women, aged 18-76 years) who completed an online survey with multiple instruments including the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2), the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness (MAIA), and other body image measures. Hierarchical regressions revealed significant predictive relationships between IA dimensions and all five facets of body image after controlling for sex, BMI, and age.

1._section_summary: This introduction section reviews body image as a multifaceted construct and explores the relationship between interoception (internal bodily sensation processing) and body image. The text discusses multiple studies examining interoceptive sensitivity and awareness in relation to body dissatisfaction and positive body image across various populations including Norwegian high school students (N=82), Hungarian university students (N=70), British female university students (N=50), Austrian nonclinical participants (N=30 each for high and low cardiac perception groups), and Australian female university students (N=200). The section emphasizes that positive body image is distinct from the absence of negative body image and highlights the limited research on relationships between interoceptive processing and positive body image specifically.
